short and long term aversive olfactory memory in the Drosophila requires cAMP signaling in distinct neuron types.
short term and long term memory in Drosophilia require cAMP signaling in different neuron types.
the short and long term memory of olfactory Pavlovian conditioning in Drosophilia require cAMP signaling in distinct neuron types.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural basis of memory and the molecular mechanisms that underlie the formation and maintenance of long-term memories.
the molecular mechanisms underlying learning and memory in the fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster.
the cellular mechanisms of associative memory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the two types of memory require cAMP signaling in different types of neurons, which may have distinct roles in memory consolidation.
the short-term memory and long-term memory in Drosophilas are mediated by cAMP signaling in distinct neuron types.
short and long term memory require cAMP signaling in different neuron types.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the two memory phases are encoded in different neuron types and that cAMP signaling in these neurons is required for the two phases of memory consolidation.
memory consolidation is not a single process but a set of processes.
short and long term memory require cAMP signaling in different neuron types, and the two memory traces can be independently consolidated.

different forms of memory can be encoded in distinct neuronal circuits.
